# Codebook

Unit: one row per firm (2000 software and engineering firms). Cross-section.

| column | description |
|---|---|
| firm_id | Firm identifier |
| remote_share | Share of engineering staff working mostly remote, 2021-2022 |
| patents_per_100_eng_2023 | Patent applications per 100 engineers in 2023 |
| log_engineers_2020 | Log number of engineers, 2020 |
| firm_age_2020 | Firm age in years, standardized, 2020 |
| patents_per_100_eng_2020 | Patent applications per 100 engineers in 2020, standardized |
| collab_index_2023 | Internal collaboration index from 2023 survey |
| region | Region (north, central, south) |
| listed | 1 if publicly listed |
| segment | Sector: hardware / software |
| vc_backed | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| founder_ceo | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| cloud_spend_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| hq_in_hub_city | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| share_phd_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| gross_margin_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
# Effect of remote work on engineering innovation

## Conclusion
The data do not support the hypothesis that more remote work raises innovation. The raw positive association is explained by pre-2021 firm characteristics. After adjusting for them, the estimated effect is small, negative and statistically indistinguishable from zero.

**Preferred estimate:** a 1 SD increase in remote_share changes patents per 100 engineers (2023) by **-0.275** (HC1 SE 0.239, p = 0.249; 95% CI about -0.74 to +0.19). The outcome has SD 10.9, so the CI rules out effects larger than about 0.07 SD in either direction.

Preferred specification: OLS of 2023 patents per 100 engineers on remote_share. Controls are all pre-period covariates: log engineers, firm age, 2020 patents, vc_backed, founder_ceo, cloud spend, hub-city HQ, PhD share, gross margin, region, listed and segment. N = 2000.

I did not adjust for collab_index_2023 in the preferred model. It is measured in 2023, after the treatment period, and remote_share strongly predicts it (coef 0.60, p < 1e-90). That makes it a post-treatment variable (a mediator or collider), and controlling for it would bias the estimate. Specification 5 shows this: the coefficient becomes -2.89, an artifact of conditioning on it.

## All specifications estimated
The coefficient on remote_share is reported with HC1 robust SEs, outcome = patents_per_100_eng_2023.

| # | Specification | Coef | SE | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Naive, no controls | 1.604 | 0.236 | 1e-11 |
| 2 | + log engineers, firm age | -0.197 | 0.236 | 0.404 |
| 3 | + 2020 patents only | 1.324 | 0.242 | 4e-8 |
| 4 | **Full pre-period controls (preferred)** | **-0.275** | **0.239** | **0.249** |
| 5 | Full controls + collab_index_2023 (post-treatment, not preferred) | -2.892 | 0.229 | 2e-36 |
| 6 | remote_share + collab_index_2023 only (not preferred) | -1.918 | 0.230 | 7e-17 |
| 7 | Full controls, remote × segment interaction | main effect (hardware) -0.421, p = 0.198; interaction (software) +0.291, p = 0.509 | | |
| 8 | Full controls, quadratic in remote_share | linear -0.280 (p = 0.240); squared -0.167 (p = 0.276) | | |
| 9 | Mediator check: collab_index_2023 on remote_share with full controls | 0.597 | | <1e-90 |

Specification 9 is not an effect on innovation. It was run only to diagnose collab_index_2023. That makes 9 regressions in total.

## Caveats
- This is a cross-section, so the estimate is causal only if the observed pre-period controls capture all confounding. Unobserved confounding could remain.
- The naive positive result (spec 1) was the one most favorable to the prior hypothesis. It is not robust: it disappears once firm size and age are controlled.
- Spec 3 stays positive because 2020 patents alone leaves size and age uncontrolled. Specs 2 and 4 show that size and age drive the raw association.

import pandas as pd, numpy as np, statsmodels.formula.api as smf
d=pd.read_csv('data.csv')
print(d.describe().T)
y='patents_per_100_eng_2023'
pre='log_engineers_2020+firm_age_2020+patents_per_100_eng_2020+vc_backed+founder_ceo+cloud_spend_2020+hq_in_hub_city+share_phd_2020+gross_margin_2020+C(region)+listed+C(segment)'
specs={
'naive':'remote_share',
'size_age':'remote_share+log_engineers_2020+firm_age_2020',
'lagged_y':'remote_share+patents_per_100_eng_2020',
'full_pre':'remote_share+'+pre,
'full_pre_plus_collab':'remote_share+collab_index_2023+'+pre,
'collab_only':'remote_share+collab_index_2023',
}
for k,v in specs.items():
    m=smf.ols(y+'~'+v,d).fit(cov_type='HC1')
    print(k,round(m.params['remote_share'],4),round(m.bse['remote_share'],4),m.pvalues['remote_share'],m.nobs)
m=smf.ols('collab_index_2023~remote_share+'+pre,d).fit(cov_type='HC1');print('collab on remote',m.params['remote_share'],m.pvalues['remote_share'])
m=smf.ols(y+'~remote_share*C(segment)+'+pre,d).fit(cov_type='HC1');print(m.params.filter(like='remote'),m.pvalues.filter(like='remote'))
m=smf.ols(y+'~remote_share+I(remote_share**2)+'+pre,d).fit(cov_type='HC1');print(m.params.filter(like='remote'),m.pvalues.filter(like='remote'))
print(d.remote_share.describe(), d[y].describe())

content.text:
I approved the report and wrote `verdict.json`.

The analyst's conclusion holds up when I re-run it. The raw positive association (1.60) disappears once pre-period controls are added. The preferred estimate of -0.275 (SE 0.239, p = 0.249) reproduces from `a.py`.

I also dropped each control in turn from the full model. Leaving out any one of the other controls leaves the estimate near -0.27 and not significant. Dropping log engineers pushes it to +1.02. Dropping firm age gives +0.12 (p = 0.62), and dropping 2020 patents gives -0.19. Firm size is the main confounder, and age and prior patents also matter.

Leaving the 2023 collaboration index out of the preferred model is justified, because it is measured after the treatment period and remote share strongly predicts it. The report also states that unobserved confounding could remain, which is the right caveat for a cross-section.
